subject: Television & Streaming
title: The Fall of Must-See TV
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Fall of Must-See TV.

hook.text: NBC's Thursday night lineup once dominated America. Seinfeld, Friends, and ER made one night appointment viewing.

buildup.text: Networks built evenings around lead-in shows. A hit at 8 PM pulled audiences into shows at 9 and 10.

discovery.text: This strategy assumed people sat in front of one TV all evening. By the 2000s, that assumption collapsed.

twist.text: Cable channels stole audiences with niche programming. HBO proved people would pay for better, edgier content.

climax.text: Must-See TV ended because viewers stopped being captive. Choice killed the captive audience.

punchline.text: Appointment TV died when viewers got options.

quiz.question: What undermined NBC's 'Must-See TV' strategy?
options: Cable channels offering niche, premium content
